text:
ria: quick heads-up: found odd UX when cancelling generator streams in the go sample app while doing token rotation. filing notes here before a PR.

ria: repro summary: start streaming with ctx, spin goroutine that calls stream.SetToken(newTok) on refresh, cancel ctx after first chunk. caller returns but background goroutine often remains for ~20s.

omar: sounds like SetToken is doing a blocking handshake or waiting on an rpc. ctx cancel won't interrupt if SetToken doesn't accept a ctx.

gabe: any stack traces? Is it a mutex wait or network IO?

ria: see snippet:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
iter := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){
  for t := range tokenC { iter.SetToken(t) }
}()
// read first token
_ = iter.Recv()
cancel()
// main returns but SetToken goroutine still stuck sometimes
```

claire: ergonomics: users expect cancel to be a hard stop. either SetToken should be nonblocking (swap pointer) OR stream should expose ForceClose/Abort that immediately tears down transport.

omar: another pattern: StreamV2 returning a handle with Done() chan and CloseNow() method. Done() closes when all internals cleaned up. That avoids leaking goroutines.

gabe: agree. Also: docs should show pattern: cancel ctx, then wait for iter.Done() before exiting process to avoid premature shutdown.

ria: i'm prototyping two things: 1) make SetToken atomic/nonblocking (store token in atomic.Value + notify send loop), 2) add StreamHandle.CloseNow() that triggers immediate transport close.

claire: test plan: add a small example under examples/stream-cancel that performs token rotation + ctx cancel and asserts no goroutines left after Done() returns. Also inject artificial server delay for handshake to ensure CloseNow aborts blocked ops.

omar: note: avoid breaking GA API surface. do StreamV2 and a compat shim Stream that wraps the new behavior for now.

gabe: thanks. when you open the draft PR, tag it devex/stream-ctxtx so bots add runtime reviewers.

ci-bot: auto-note: add a CHANGELOG entry and a short onboarding snippet: "To interrupt a generator: cancel ctx, wait on iter.Done() or call iter.CloseNow() for immediate teardown."

ria: will do. i'll add the example and tests and post PR link here.
